  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The merge-commit lookup comment says the first matching commit is the oldest, but `git log` without `--reverse` is newest-first.
  WHY: In a future multi-merge/revert scenario, the code could capture the wrong merge timestamp and purge a valid entry.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~2165-2215 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The purge loop only considers the first commit matching the PR reference, so multiple mentions of the same `(#PR)` can select the wrong merge timestamp.
  WHY: Wrong timestamp selection can keep a stale entry or purge a healthy one.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_purge_stale_fingerprint_entries_on_integration_branch | severity=medium | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The suffix check requires the subject to end with `(#<pr>)` exactly, so trailing whitespace/CR or other subject normalization can make a real merge commit fail the purge predicate.
  WHY: The code can miss stale entries even when `git log --grep` finds the PR reference elsewhere in history.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~14375-14385 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The state file is mutated in place without any locking, so overlapping pollers can race while rewriting `merged_issue_fingerprints`.
  WHY: Concurrent writes can corrupt the JSON state or lose fingerprint entries, breaking the verifier.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~2195-2200 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `date -u -d "${captured_at}"` can fail on malformed or non-GNU date inputs, and the code falls back to keeping the entry.
  WHY: Edge-case timestamps will be treated as non-stale, leaving phantom entries in place.
- tests/test_fingerprint_state_selfheal.py:~80,~130,~170 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The test helpers and `_purged()` parser are fragile to output-format changes and subjects containing tabs/newlines.
  WHY: Small formatting changes could make the test suite fail or give false positives.
- tests/test_fingerprint_state_selfheal.py:~480-506 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The standalone test runner uses plain `assert` checks, so one failure aborts the rest of the suite.
  WHY: A single broken test hides the remaining results in CI output.

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_purge_stale_fingerprint_entries_on_integration_branch() lines ~2165-2215 and invocation at ~14385 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function correctly identifies stale entries using `git log --grep` + committer date comparison and mutates state via `jq | mv`, but the inner loop only considers the first matching commit for the merge timestamp.
  WHY: If multiple commits mention the same `(#PR)` (e.g. backport + rebase + merge), it may pick the wrong (older) one and either keep a stale entry or purge a healthy one.
- tests/test_fingerprint_state_selfheal.py lines ~130, ~170, and ~80 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Test harness relies on `git commit-tree` with crafted subjects and exact timestamp control, and `_purged()` does a naive `.split("\t")` with no error handling for malformed output.
  WHY: Subjects containing tabs/newlines or slight formatting changes can make the tests flaky or produce false positives.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines ~14375-14385 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: State file is mutated in-place with no lock while the orchestrator poller can run concurrently on multiple workers or overlapping cron invocations.
  WHY: A race between pollers could corrupt the JSON state file or lose fingerprint entries, leading to jq errors or lost protection.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines ~2195-2200 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `date -u -d "${captured_at}" +%s` can fail silently on non-ISO or otherwise malformed dates, and the code treats that as non-stale.
  WHY: Edge-case timestamps are kept instead of purged, which can perpetuate phantom gate failures.
- tests/test_fingerprint_state_selfheal.py lines ~480-506 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The tests use `assert` statements directly, so a single failure aborts the rest of the suite under plain `python3`.
  WHY: One broken test hides the remaining results in CI output instead of reporting all failures.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
